title: Redwood May 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly all-hands covering Q2 priorities, product roadmap updates (Dedicated/Private features), hiring plans, performance metrics, and a security/compliance update. Leadership recapped progress on Dedicated capacity and Private deployments, shared customer stories, and answered questions about cost/latency tradeoffs and regulatory readiness. Several action items: publish Q2 priorities doc, schedule focused product deep-dive, and share updated SOC2/ISO timeline.

transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands - May 20 2026 | 16:00 - 16:58 UTC | Duration 58m
Attendees: Ira Kaplan, Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Samir Patel, Maya Lopez, Jordan Reed, Leah Kim + company

Summary (auto): Quick updates from leadership, product roadmap highlights, Dedicated & Private progress, hiring and org notes, security/compliance update, open Q&A.

[00:00] Ira Kaplan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll kick off, um, on time. Quick housekeeping — this will be recorded, slides up on the wiki, please hold questions for the end or drop in chat.
[00:28] Alex Chen: Quick note on uptime — last month we hit 99.95% for Hosted API, and Dedicated throughput improved after the kernel selection changes; latency p50 down about 12%. Some of the tail still needs work, we'll cover that in the infra section.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Product highlights — we've shipped streaming tool calling for the hosted API, and the Private preview included KMS integration for a handful of customers. There were some, uh, minor regressions in token accounting we patched last week.
[01:40] Ira Kaplan: Great, thanks. On business — renewal motion is strong, especially with the Dedicated offering. Jordan, quick update on sales?
[02:05] Jordan Reed: Yeah, pipeline healthy. A few mid-market deals coming up for Dedicated, and a couple of larger prospects asked for Private (V P C + on-prem) references. We ran a benchmark spreadsheet with one retailer that showed 27% cost savings vs their self-host baseline when using our batching/caching suggestions, so that's resonating.
[02:40] Samir Patel: On the infra side, we've rolled out continuous batching changes to reduce variance. There's still a scenario where long-seq requests push the KV cache memory, um, and cause slight thrash; we're working a mitigation -> smarter eviction policy.
[03:10] Audience (microphone): Quick question about quantization support in Private — are we recommending 4-bit vs 8-bit for customers on smaller fleets?
[03:35] Alex Chen: Good question. We recommend 4-bit for inference cost savings when latency SLOs allow; 8-bit is safer for some models. Our runtime has a quantization-friendly execution path but there are model-specific tradeoffs. We'll publish a more prescriptive guide in the next week.
[04:05] Priya Nair: Roadmap: For Q2 we're focusing on three things — 1) improving runtime tail latency, 2) stronger Private onboarding docs & installers, 3) observability exports that make cost attribution per-route easier.
[05:00] Maya Lopez: Org update — hiring remains a priority for Eng and Product, we're opening 14 roles this quarter; we'll also run an internal recruiter AMA next week. No company-level hiring freeze planned.
[05:30] Leah Kim: Marketing — we'll push customer case studies next month, plus a benchmarking blog post. If product folks have concise results (numbers + config) please drop them in the marketing channel.
[06:10] Ira Kaplan: Security update — good progress on SOC 2. We're tracking ISO and some EU data residency asks; Security will publish a timeline.
[06:35] Alex Chen: Technical note: KV cache was transcribed in a few tickets as "k v cache" so apologies for the odd spacing in some docs; also some references to SAML were mis-said as "sammel" in one recording — human transcriptions are imperfect.
[07:05] Audience Q: Any changes to pricing or cost model?
[07:20] Ira Kaplan: No immediate pricing changes — focus is on giving customers levers to tune cost: batching, caching, quantization profiles, and routing policies. For enterprise Dedicated contracts we'll continue to do fixed committed capacity options.
[08:00] Jordan Reed: We got a question from a prospect about multi-region fallbacks and graceful degradation — the platform supports automated fallback to compatible model variants, and routing by latency or cost. We'll prepare a reference architecture doc for sales.
[09:10] Priya Nair: Product demos coming up — we'll have a dedicated session on Private deployments and one on the new streaming/func call features. Sign-ups will be in the events channel.
[10:00] Samir Patel: On performance: our kernel selection improvements helped p50 and p90 on A100 class hardware and some of the newer chips. We still see worse p99 on long-context workloads. Plan is targeted micro-optimizations + better prefetching of KV cache.
[12:30] Audience: Question about audit logs and KMS/H S M support for customers in regulated industries.
[12:50] Alex Chen: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can discuss H S M options for on-prem pilots; audit logs are part of Redwood Private. Security will publish a FAQ.
[14:00] Maya Lopez: People ops — remember benefits open enrollment reminder next month; we also ran a pulse survey, results will go out later this week.
[15:10] Ira Kaplan: Financials: topline is tracking, we saw M M R growth quarter-over-quarter; cost discipline remains important — Samir's team is focused on improving unit economics for both hosted and Dedicated.
[16:00] Jordan Reed: On renewals, timeline for one large customer moved up — we'll need SE support for a POC earlier than expected, asking PMs & Eng for assistance.
[18:00] Audience: Question on private vs dedicated — what should a customer choose?
[18:22] Priya Nair: Quick guide: Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation with a Redwood-managed infra; Private when customers need V P C or on-prem, or strict data residency/compliance. There are tradeoffs (ops burden vs control).
[19:10] Alex Chen: Also worth noting Dedicated has burst capacity options and SLAs; Private is more complex but gives full control over network and keys.
[20:00] Audience member (Engineer): Any guidance for dev teams migrating from self-host to Redwood?
[20:20] Samir Patel: We have a migration checklist — start with small QPS tests, run the benchmark harness, measure beam throughput and latency with your typical prompts; use our autoscaling and routing policies. We'll publish the checklist link after this meeting.
[21:30] Leah Kim: Marketing note: please review the customer quotes in the drive, email any suggested edits.
[22:05] Ira Kaplan: Ok open Q&A — drop questions or raise hands.
[22:35] Audience: Is there an internal plan for offsite or team retreats this summer?
[22:50] Maya Lopez: Yes, planning a regional meetup in July and a company offsite in September, details coming.
[24:05] Audience: Any exec changes? I heard rumors about a new hire in product leadership.
[24:20] Ira Kaplan: We added Priya as Head of Product last month (official intro in April), and we'll post a full org chart soon. No other exec changes planned.
[25:00] Audience: Question about benchmarks — are we sharing benchmark artifacts publically?
[25:18] Alex Chen: We'll publish sanitized benchmark results and a methodology doc; raw customer data stays private.
[26:30] Jordan Reed: Sales highlight: won a multi-year deal with a fintech prospect by leaning into our observability and compliance posture.
[28:00] Priya Nair: Product deep-dive will include canary and A/B rollout controls in the Console — those are coming in beta this quarter.
[30:10] Samir Patel: Reminder to SEs: when you onboard Dedicated customers please capture per-route token cost breakdowns in the onboarding doc.
[32:05] Audience: What's the plan for open-source model support? Any commitment to specific model families?
[32:25] Alex Chen: We'll continue to curate a model catalog with verified performance profiles; no exclusive lock to any single family. We optimize kernels and quantization profiles per architecture.
[34:00] Ira Kaplan: Quick customer story — retailer saved ops cost using caching, moved into Dedicated for predictable promos traffic. Good showcase for marketing.
[35:10] Leah Kim: We'll coordinate that case study — product to share anonymized numbers.
[36:40] Audience: Security question: backup retention and data residency for EU customers?
[36:55] Alex Chen: For Private we support customer-controlled storage locations; for Hosted we offer region pinning and data retention options. Security will share specifics.
[38:20] Priya Nair: Quick demo schedule reminder — sign up, seats limited for hands-on private previews.
[39:05] Audience: Are we targeting any new verticals?
[39:20] Jordan Reed: Finance and retail are strong, also healthcare interest but requires more compliance work.
[40:10] Maya Lopez: People ops note — manager training sessions next month, please RSVP.
[41:00] Ira Kaplan: Alright last 15 minutes — lightning updates from teams.
[41:20] Samir Patel: Batch improvements rolled to prod; kernel selection autotuner in internal canary.
[41:45] Alex Chen: Observability exports for cost attribution in beta.
[42:10] Priya Nair: Private installer improvements — reduced installer time for on-prem from 6 hours to about 90 minutes in our test.
[43:00] Leah Kim: Sales enablement content published for Dedicated.
[43:30] Jordan Reed: New pricing page updated with committed capacity options.
[44:00] Audience: Quick Q about legal — any update on contract templates for Private?
[44:20] Ira Kaplan: Legal is rolling out updated contract templates for Private and Dedicated, will post in the legal channel.
[45:10] Audience: What's the status of our partner program?
[45:25] Alex Chen: Partner pilot with a cloud reseller is live in two regions; still early.
[46:00] Priya Nair: Closing notes — product will run two office hours sessions next week for deeper technical Qs.
[46:30] Ira Kaplan: Thanks everyone. Recap of actions: publish Q2 priorities doc, roadmap slides, schedule deep-dive, infra to share cost/latency analysis. We'll follow up in the #all-hands-followup channel.
[47:15] Audience: Thanks, Ira.
[56:30] Meeting ends.
